candidates.changed_node: 1 - CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) / ($leverage + 1e-8)) - a level-deflated gate replacing both parents' additive leverage legs
candidates.rationale: A donates $roa - $accrual_gap, B donates TS_DELTA($leverage, 63). Both parents are additive: each ranks a quality leg and a leverage-change leg and subtracts them. The child makes the leverage change a conditioning variable instead of a leg, so accrual-adjusted profitability is pulled toward zero in names that are levering up, and it deflates the change by the leverage level so the same absolute delta counts for less at an already-levered firm. Neither parent has that interaction: A scales its leverage delta by a price ratio, B leaves it unscaled, and neither lets it modulate the quality signal.

candidates.changed_node: TS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 252) grafted into B's multiplicative shell, with the normaliser changed to TS_MEAN($high - $low, 42)
candidates.rationale: A donates TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), B donates $high - $low and its accrual rank. B uses a price term as a trigger for a fundamental score, but its score is accruals alone; A says balance-sheet expansion is the other half of the same deterioration. The child sums the two into one score, both on a 0-1 scale (cross-sectional rank of accruals, time-series rank of the leverage change against its own year, which keeps a quarterly-stamped field off the cross-section), and multiplies by today's range relative to that stock's own 42-day mean range. The new element is that the fundamental signal only fires on days the name is actually moving, and the range is normalised per-stock rather than against a 21-day high anchor.

candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK(TS_CORR($high - $low, $dollar_volume, 42)) becomes a multiplier on CS_RANK($accrual_gap) - CS_RANK($roe) instead of an additive term
candidates.rationale: A donates $high - $low and its accrual rank, B donates the ROE rank and the range-versus-turnover correlation. B subtracts that correlation from quality, treating it as a second additive signal; A multiplies accruals by a contemporaneous range with no volume in it at all. The child turns the correlation into a participation gate on a two-sided quality spread (accruals minus profitability): the fundamental spread is expressed only where the daily range is genuinely explained by turnover, i.e. where a marginal trader is present to reprice the name. That is an interaction, not a third leg, and it is what neither parent captures.

candidates.changed_node: CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($close, 42) / (TS_MEAN($close, 3) + 1e-8)) - B's reversal recast scale-free and applied multiplicatively to A's rank spread
candidates.rationale: A donates $high - $low inside its range/volume correlation, B donates TS_MEAN($close, 3). A's quality leg is ROE, B's is an earnings yield. The child keeps A's value-minus-impact rank spread but swaps in B's yield so both legs of the spread are priced quantities, then multiplies by B's short-horizon reversal rewritten scale-free as a 42-day over 3-day price ratio (positive when the name has just sold off). The fusion is timing: the value-minus-impact spread is slow and has no entry rule, the reversal is fast and has no anchor, and the product buys cheap, low-impact names specifically on their weak days.

candidates.changed_node: B's correlation rank lifted into the IF_ELSE condition, switching the sign of A's EMA($close, 10) deviation
candidates.rationale: A donates EMA($close, 10), B donates $high - $low inside its volume/range correlation. B is a standalone microstructure rank with no return signal; A is a reversal with no regime test. The child uses B as a switch rather than a score: in the top half of the correlation rank the range is volume-explained, the move is order-flow driven, and it is faded in A's reversal orientation; in the bottom half the move is information and is followed instead. The sign flip is the fusion. Neither parent can change the sign of its own signal, and a multiplicative weight could not do it either, which is also why this child does not simply track A.

candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42)) replaces B's CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8)) as the scaler, and the leverage delta is clipped at zero
candidates.rationale: B donates CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), A donates $high - $low inside its volume/range correlation. B already scales its leverage penalty by a price term, but that term is relative range, a plain volatility proxy: a wide bar counts the same whether it came from an overnight gap or from being traded through. Substituting A's correlation makes the penalty conditional on the range being volume-explained, which is the distinction B cannot draw. The MAX(..., 0) is the second half of the fusion: only leverage increases are penalised, so a deleveraging firm does not turn the range term into a spurious long.

candidates.changed_node: B's downside-volatility ratio replaced by A's demeaned quality-minus-leverage-build spread as the multiplier on momentum
candidates.rationale: A donates CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), B donates TS_SUM($return, 68). B scales momentum by a downside-volatility share computed from the very returns that produced the momentum, so its conditioner carries no independent information. The child replaces it with A's fundamental health spread, profitability minus leverage build, both demeaned so they subtract on a common scale, and multiplies. That signs the momentum: a run-up in a deleveraging, profitable name is kept, the identical run-up in one levering up is shorted. Neither parent can separate those two cases, because A has no return term and B has no balance sheet.

candidates.changed_node: CS_ZSCORE(TS_STD(MIN($return, 0), 42)) inserted as a risk multiplier, and B's TS_MAX($high, 21) - $low denominator widened to TS_MAX($high, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 42)
candidates.rationale: A donates MIN($return, 0), B donates CS_RANK($accrual_gap), $high - $low and TS_MAX($high, 21). B multiplies accrual quality by a range position and so treats every high-accrual name as equally exposed; A's semi-deviation identifies which names actually carry the left tail. The child inserts downside volatility between the two, concentrating the accrual short in names whose realised return distribution is already skewed down, and widens B's denominator from a distance to one day's low into a full 21/42-day high-low band so the range term reads as a share of the recent trading range. The fusion is accrual quality times crash exposure times range participation: A supplies the risk axis B lacks.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
